q01.question: Is editor harm more than a repeated evaluation produces?
q01.answer: Yes. In 1.8–2.3% of pairs a repeated base run fails where the first run succeeded; the 112-task editors harm 4.8–5.7% (L2) to 10.2–10.9% (L3) of pairs.

q02.question: Do the recipe differences hold across training seeds?
q02.answer: At 16 source tasks, L3 is below L1 and L2 in all three seeds. At 112 source tasks and 121.25k updates, L1 and L2 exceed L3 in all three seeds; L2 stays consistent (58.11–60.28%), L3 seed 2 (46.44%) matches seed 0 (46.78%) while seed 1 is lower (34.83%), and L1 reaches 61.28% in seed 2.

q03.question: Does transfer extend beyond the 18 held-out tasks?
q03.answer: Yes. On 96 further unseen tasks the 16-task L1 and L2 editors raise SR from 19.15% to 40.94% and 40.71%; L3 reaches 28.58%.

q04.question: Is transfer higher where source experience is closer?
q04.answer: For the 16-task L1 and L2 editors on the 96 tasks, gain falls as feature distance to source contexts rises (Spearman −0.37 and −0.33); for L3 the interval includes zero.

q05.question: Does a smaller correction help every recipe?
q05.answer: Yes for the three 112-task editors: half scale changes held-out SR by +4.39, +3.39 and +8.94 points for L1, L2 and L3, and lowers harm for all three.

q06.question: Do the arm and the gripper correction respond alike to scaling?
q06.answer: No. For the 112-task L3 editor, halving the arm correction raises held-out SR by 10.28 points and halving the gripper correction lowers it by 10.28 points.

q07.question: Do source correction directions explain held-out corrections for every recipe?
q07.answer: For the 112-task editors, ten source directions capture 85.3% of held-out correction variance for L3, 76.1% for L2 and 68.8% for L1.

q08.question: Do context-dependent gates exceed uniform scaling?
q08.answer: No. None of the support, magnitude-cap or cross-recipe disagreement gates exceeds uniform scaling at its own mean scale; cross-recipe gating falls below uniform scaling for L3 (−2.63 points) and the mean ensemble (−4.85 points).

q09.question: Does narrow-source negative transfer hold for every recipe?
q09.answer: Yes. Two-source L1 and L2 also drop below the base on the 18 held-out tasks (5.44% and 19.72%, against 1.00% for L3), despite 87–94% source SR.

q10.question: Does held-out transfer appear early for the soft-penalty recipes?
q10.answer: Yes. L1 and L2 reach 52.00% and 52.89% held-out SR at 51.25k updates (46.33–56.72% across added seeds). L2 is highest near 121k updates and lower at its endpoint, so the L1–L2 order depends on training length and seed.

q11.question: Do expert routing, the editor's instruction, or the camera input change held-out transfer?
q11.answer: Routing: single runs do not establish an effect. Instruction: SR changes by at most 1.67 points for any recipe. Camera: with the main camera only, none of the three 16-task encoder editors (L1, L2 or L3) exceeds its readout counterpart.

q12.question: Does pretraining speed adaptation under the soft-penalty recipes?
q12.answer: Not consistently. Pretraining lowers online critic loss by 45–60% across all three targets (including Task 39), but pretrained and fresh runs are level from 5k updates and lose source SR without replay.
